Confirmed the cause: `displayName` dereferences `user.name` without a null check, so `displayName(null)` throws and `displayName({})` returns `undefined` instead of `"anonymous"`. Let me verify with the test runner, then fix.

Fixed. The `null-guard` test passes now.

**Cause:** `displayName` in `packages/shared/src/format.js` unconditionally did `user.name.trim()`, so:
- `displayName(null)` threw `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'name')`
- `displayName({})` would return `undefined` instead of `"anonymous"`

**Fix:**
```js
export function displayName(user) {
  const name = user?.name?.trim();
  return name || "anonymous";
}
```
Optional chaining guards both the null user and the missing/empty name (the `||` also covers a whitespace-only name, since `.trim()` yields `""`), while existing behavior for real names — including trimming — is unchanged (`"  Ada Lovelace "` still passes).

Test run confirms: `[null-guard]` is `ok`, 7 passing / 2 failing. The remaining failures (`cli-flag`, `timezone`) are the other intentionally-seeded bugs per the README, untouched as out of scope.

The bug: `dayKey` groups by UTC days per its doc comment, but uses local-time getters (`getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate`). With `TZ=America/New_York`, `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` falls on Jan 1 local time, yielding `2026-01-01` instead of `2026-01-02`.

Fixed. The test now passes.

**Cause:** `dayKey()` in `packages/shared/src/dates.js` claims to group events by calendar day in UTC but used local-time accessors (`getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate`). Under the test's `TZ=America/New_York`, the instant `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` is still Jan 1 locally, so it returned `2026-01-01`.

**Fix:** Swapped to the UTC equivalents — `getUTCFullYear`/`getUTCMonth`/`getUTCDate`.

The other two intentionally failing tests (`cli-flag`, `null-guard`) mentioned in the README are untouched, as you only asked about `timezone`.
